entries.description: Harry and Lupin recall that a Grindylow in a tank stood in a corner of Lupin’s office on Harry’s first visit.
entries.model_notes: Recollection used for an identity check and accepted by Lupin; establishes tank-to-corner relationship but no size, window, floor or later survival of the fixture.

entries.description: Harry recalls private hours with Ginny in secluded corners of the school grounds. At the wedding he again remembers afternoons with her in lonely parts of the grounds.
entries.model_notes: Narrated memory of outdoor privacy/concealment opportunities; no named corner, wall, planting type or exact spot is described.

entries.description: Harry recalls Barty Crouch being Transfigured into a bone and buried in Hagrid’s front garden.
entries.model_notes: Reported recollection, not a visible grave or current inspection. Parent should reconcile this wording with the original event’s evidence; no marker, exact position or remaining bone is described.

entries.location: Library Horcrux books removed to Headmaster study
entries.description: Hermione says Dumbledore removed all Horcrux books from the library shelves without destroying them, keeping them in his study. One recovered volume, Secrets of the Darkest Art, is large and bound in faded black leather.
entries.model_notes: Collection/storage state before funeral and subsequent removal; exact office shelf/cabinet is not identified and the time of original removal is explicitly uncertain.

entries.description: Hermione reports Summoning the removed books after Dumbledore’s funeral: they flew out of his study window and into the girls’ dormitory through its open window, where she packed them.
entries.temporal: Immediately after June 1997 funeral, reported July 1997
entries.model_notes: Exterior aerial connection and opening dormitory window. No window-to-window distance, compass bearing or full flight path specified; do not assume adjacent rooms.

entries.description: Hagrid reports that there are newborn unicorns and offers to show the students when they return.
entries.model_notes: Dated animal-population state associated with Hagrid’s Hogwarts work; exact enclosure or Forest clearing unspecified.

entries.location: Dumbledore’s library and instruments bequeathed to school
entries.description: Scrimgeour says Dumbledore’s private library, magical instruments and most other personal effects were left to Hogwarts.
entries.model_notes: Disposition supports continued school ownership of the collection; no physical relocation or exact posthumous room arrangement is shown here.

entries.location: Gryffindor sword and Sorting Hat presentation
entries.description: Hermione recalls the sword coming to Harry out of the Sorting Hat. Scrimgeour says historical sources allow it to present itself to any worthy Gryffindor and refuses to transfer it under Dumbledore’s will. Harry recalls it hanging on the office wall during the previous year’s lessons.
entries.model_notes: Reported access behaviour and former display position, not proof of a current item’s authenticity or a visible sword-to-hat passage. No sword is produced at this meeting.

entries.description: Seeing Phineas Nigellus’s empty portrait at Grimmauld Place, Harry concludes that its subject is spending the night in the Headmaster’s study at Hogwarts.
entries.model_notes: Establishes Harry’s understanding of linked portrait destinations; his conclusion is not a direct observation of the school frame that night.

entries.description: Ron explains that house-elves can Apparate and Disapparate into and out of Hogwarts although wizards cannot.
entries.model_notes: Species-specific access rule; do not apply the wizard prohibition to house-elves. The sea cave discussed alongside it is a separate remote site.

entries.description: Harry remembers following the scarlet steam engine by air as it passed between fields and hills.
entries.temporal: Recollection on 1 September 1997 of an earlier school journey
entries.model_notes: Rural railway landscape, not a surveyed immediate castle approach; no distances or exact segment identified.

entries.description: The Headmaster’s office is a circular room at the top of a tower. Harry associates it with Dumbledore’s delicate silver instruments, stone Pensieve, Sorting Hat and the sword of Gryffindor, whose continued presence he is unsure of.
entries.temporal: Remembered office on 1 September 1997; Snape’s occupation anticipated
entries.model_notes: Room form and remembered contents are narrated; Harry is imagining Snape there and explicitly allows that the sword may have moved. Do not treat this as a witnessed inventory under Snape.

entries.description: Phineas Nigellus can move between his framed portrait at Grimmauld Place and the one hanging in the Headmaster’s office. Hermione puts the portable frame in her enlarged handbag to prevent its subject seeing the house for Snape.
entries.model_notes: Linked portrait travel and visual access depend on frame placement; no physical tunnel implied.

entries.description: Harry recognises the Ministry office as matching Umbridge’s Hogwarts office: lace draperies, doilies and dried flowers covering surfaces, ornamental wall plates with brightly coloured beribboned moving kittens, and a flouncy flowered desk cloth.
entries.temporal: Recollection in September 1997 of Umbridge’s 1995–96 Hogwarts office
entries.model_notes: The explicit comparison supports these shared decorations; the Ministry door’s transplanted magical eye and telescope are not stated to have been at Hogwarts.

entries.description: A Ministry filing cabinet reminds Harry of Filch’s filing cabinets at Hogwarts, full of folders labelled with individual names.
entries.temporal: Recollection in September 1997 of Umbridge’s 1995–96 Hogwarts office
entries.model_notes: Confirms cabinets and folder organisation, without assigning their room position or number.

entries.description: Harry initially mistakes another wood for the Forbidden Forest and imagines slipping through its trees to Hagrid’s hut. He distinguishes the other wood by its younger, more widely spaced trees and clearer ground.
entries.model_notes: Relative comparison supports older, denser trees and more obstructed ground in the Forbidden Forest, not uniform tree ages or measured spacing. The observed canopy and clearing belong to the World Cup woods, not Hogwarts.

entries.description: Dirk reports that Ginny and two friends entered Snape’s office, smashed the sword’s glass case and were caught carrying the sword down the staircase. He says Snape sent the displayed sword to Gringotts a couple of days later; Griphook identifies that deposited blade as a copy.
entries.model_notes: Reported chain is Bill to Griphook to Dirk; preserve broken case and removed display as dated states. This does not establish who made the substitution or when.

entries.description: Hermione says Phineas Nigellus’s portrait hangs immediately beside the sword’s display case.
entries.model_notes: Relative adjacency, without compass direction or height.

entries.description: Phineas Nigellus explains that Hogwarts portraits can communicate with one another, but may leave the castle only to visit another painting of themselves. Dumbledore therefore cannot accompany him into his frame outside Hogwarts.
entries.model_notes: Castle boundary limits portrait travel; the painted subject can move to a linked self-portrait and remains able to hear while blindfolded. Do not permit unrestricted travel through arbitrary off-site portraits. A later explicit comparison with Luna’s painted ceiling confirms that Hogwarts portraits move.

entries.description: Phineas reports that Snape sent Ginny, Neville and Luna into the Forbidden Forest to work for Hagrid. Ron subsequently protests that the forest contains giant spiders.
entries.model_notes: Dated use as detention/work area and character report of dangerous fauna; no work site or route within the forest is specified.

entries.description: In speculating where the sword might be hidden, Harry says nobody goes into the Shrieking Shack; Hermione points out that Snape knows how to enter it.
entries.model_notes: Statements concern secluded access and a known entrant, not proof the sword was stored there or a description of its entrance.

entries.description: From remote camps Harry uses the Marauder’s Map to watch for Ron in Hogwarts corridors and to see Ginny’s name in the girls’ dormitory.
entries.model_notes: Remote live tracking includes corridors and a girls’ dormitory; no room shape or absolute position supplied.

entries.description: Phineas Nigellus reports that Ginny is banned from visiting Hogsmeade under Snape. Harry also remembers needing a guardian-signed permission slip and asking McGonagall for permission when he lacked one.
entries.temporal: Autumn 1997 restriction and recollection of earlier visits
entries.model_notes: Social access constraints for the village route, without a newly described physical barrier.

entries.description: Carols recall Hogwarts Christmases to Harry: twelve Christmas trees in the Great Hall and Peeves singing rude carols from inside suits of armour.
entries.temporal: Christmas Eve 1997 recollection of earlier school Christmases
entries.model_notes: Seasonal count and use of hollow armour; no assertion that the same decorations are present under Snape that year.

entries.description: Harry identifies his parents’ white-marble headstone as the same material as Dumbledore’s tomb.
entries.model_notes: Corroborates the Hogwarts tomb’s white marble only; graveyard row positions and visibility belong to Godric’s Hollow, not the school tomb.

entries.location: Room of Requirement / hidden objects state
entries.description: The clutter of Xenophilius’s living room recalls the Room of Requirement transformed into a gigantic labyrinth made of objects hidden over centuries.
entries.temporal: Late December 1997 recollection of the 1996–97 hiding-room state
entries.model_notes: Supports enormous scale and maze-like accumulated storage. The circular room, hanging creature models and working printing press belong to Lovegood’s house and are not attributes of the Hogwarts room.

entries.description: Potterwatch reports Hagrid escaping attempted arrest within the grounds after a rumoured pro-Harry gathering in his house. Lee refers to his sixteen-foot-high half-brother as possible help in the escape.
entries.temporal: March 1998 broadcast about events within the previous hours
entries.model_notes: Evidence for an inhabited Hagrid house after the previous book’s fire, without a stated reconstruction or a guarantee it is the same building. The party is explicitly a rumour; Grawp’s assistance is suggested rather than witnessed.

entries.description: Harry tells the Snatchers that the Slytherin common room is in the dungeons, entered through a wall, full of skulls and other things, and under the lake, which gives its light a green colour.
entries.temporal: March 1998 account of remembered school space
entries.model_notes: Harry is falsely claiming Slytherin membership; Scabior accepts the architectural answer as convincing. Retain the account as reported rather than a witnessed current state. No window form, lake depth or entrance password supplied.

entries.location: Tallest tower / lawn at its foot
entries.description: Dobby’s death recalls Harry kneeling beside Dumbledore’s body on the grass at the foot of Hogwarts’ tallest tower.
entries.model_notes: Confirms highest-tower base on lawn; no new tower plan or height.

entries.description: Harry remembers rows and rows of golden chairs at Dumbledore’s funeral, the Minister for Magic in the front row, and a stately white marble tomb.
entries.model_notes: Adds chair colour and seating arrangement. The rough earth grave and bushes described in the present scene belong to Dobby’s remote Shell Cottage burial.

entries.description: In the dawn vision, Hogsmeade’s main street remains dark while the sun has already risen at Shell Cottage; the narration attributes the difference to its position much farther north.
entries.model_notes: Narrated relative geography, not a usable numerical latitude, travel distance or astronomical measurement.

entries.location: Hogwarts gates → grounds → lakeshore → castle path
entries.description: Harry sees Voldemort at the school gates as a lamp approaches through the pre-dawn. He then experiences travel alongside Snape up through the grounds towards the lake. Snape returns up the path towards the castle; Voldemort continues around the lake edge, with the castle in view and no lights in its windows.
entries.model_notes: Narrated through Harry’s connection to Voldemort. Preserve the sequence and uphill wording without assuming the exact junction of the lake path and entrance drive.

entries.description: The white marble tomb stands beside the lake and is reflected in its dark water. Voldemort splits it open lengthwise from head to foot, revealing a shrouded, long thin body; the wrappings open and the wand is removed from beneath the folded hands on its chest.
entries.model_notes: Dated open/broken state, not the intact funeral model. No lid thickness, cavity dimensions or repair yet established.

entries.description: In Harry’s vision Voldemort believes Harry cannot enter Hogsmeade undetected, still less the school, and plans to alert Snape that he may try to re-enter the castle. Harry chooses Hogsmeade as the approach from which to assess the school’s protections.
entries.temporal: May 1998, immediately before the return to Hogwarts
entries.model_notes: The impossibility is Voldemort’s confidence, not an established absolute barrier. Protection mechanisms are not described here; preserve subsequent observations separately.

entries.description: On arrival Harry sees dark shop fronts, black mountains beyond the village, the curve in the road ahead leading towards Hogwarts, and light from the Three Broomsticks. They retreat from the High Street into the nearest narrow side street.
entries.model_notes: Local street curve and mountain backdrop without compass bearing. Three Broomsticks functions as a Death Eater base that night.

entries.description: Their night arrival causes a piercing scream, which a Death Eater silences with his wand. The Death Eaters call it a Caterwauling Charm enforcing curfew; Aberforth says moving outdoors in darkness triggers it and that curfew lifts at daybreak.
entries.model_notes: Observed alarm plus attributed explanation. The alarm detects an outdoor presence despite the Invisibility Cloak; it does not itself identify the trio’s exact position.

entries.description: The trio cannot Disapparate: the air feels solid. Dementors draw light from the surroundings and stars, bring intense cold, and approach around a corner of the side street, ten or more appearing darker than the darkness. A Patronus drives them away and the stars return.
entries.model_notes: Dated town restriction and environmental effect, not proof of permanent year-round town anti-Apparition rules.

entries.location: Hog’s Head side entrance → upstairs sitting room
entries.description: A bolted door opens on the left side of the narrow street into the Hog’s Head’s grubby, sawdust-strewn bar, lit by one flickering candle. Behind the counter a second doorway leads to a rickety wooden staircase opening into the upstairs sitting room.
entries.model_notes: Tunnel access approach; relative left is from the trio’s retreat, not a compass direction. The upstairs grimy window overlooks the street.

entries.location: Hog’s Head upstairs sitting room / tunnel anteroom
entries.description: The sitting room has a threadbare carpet, small fireplace, wobble-legged chair and a small table before the fire. One large oil painting of a blonde girl hangs above the fireplace; it is the room’s only picture. A small rectangular mirror stands on the mantelpiece directly below it. Harry closes the window curtains; Aberforth lights lamps and the fire.
entries.model_notes: Necessary model context for tunnel mouth. Mirror is a communication object, separate from the passage portrait; no Albus photograph is present.

entries.description: Aberforth advises waiting until daylight, leaving Hogsmeade on foot and climbing into the mountains, where Apparition becomes possible. He reports Hagrid hiding in a cave there with Grawp after the attempted arrest.
entries.model_notes: No surveyed town boundary, cave coordinates or identity with the earlier mountain cave supplied.

entries.location: Hogwarts boundary walls / old passages / patrols
entries.description: Aberforth reports all old secret passages watched at both ends, Dementors around the boundary walls, and regular patrols within the school; he says his alternative is now the only way in.
entries.model_notes: His sources support a very heavily guarded wartime state; “only” is his assessment, not a guarantee against every magical exception.

entries.location: Hog’s Head Ariana portrait / real tunnel entrance
entries.description: Ariana’s painted figure walks away into a long dark tunnel depicted behind her, then returns with Neville. The whole picture swings forwards like a little door, revealing a real tunnel. Neville climbs out and jumps down from the mantelpiece.
entries.model_notes: Portrait aperture is above the fireplace/mantelpiece; the painted approach depicts the real tunnel’s traveller. Far endpoint and dimensions await the next chapter.

entries.description: Aberforth says the Caterwauling Charm covers the entire village. Neville explains that arriving allies will Apparate directly into the Hog’s Head bar.
entries.model_notes: Indoor arrival is offered despite failed outdoor Disapparition in chapter 28. Preserve that distinction; do not infer a universal town-wide ban on every direction or destination of Apparition.

entries.location: Hog’s Head → Room of Requirement tunnel
entries.description: Beyond the portrait are smooth stone steps and a worn, smooth earthy floor, with brass wall lamps casting moving shadows. The passage later slopes steeply uphill, turns a corner, and ends at a short flight of steps and a small door like the portrait aperture, opening into the Room of Requirement.
entries.model_notes: Apparently aged surfaces do not prove age: Neville says the passage appeared recently. No length or compass bearing given.

entries.description: Neville says all the seven old school passages had been sealed before the school year began, with curses over entrances and Death Eaters and Dementors at exits.
entries.model_notes: Dated 1997–98 closures; number seven is Ron’s understanding, accepted in Neville’s reply. Do not confuse this new passage, absent from the Map discussion, with one of the old seven.

entries.description: Neville reports Dumbledore’s Army sneaking out at night to put recruitment graffiti on the walls, angering Snape.
entries.model_notes: No corridor or inscription location identified. Physical wartime wall markings, not a permanent decorative layer.

entries.location: Room of Requirement / resistance refuge interior
entries.description: The enormous refuge resembles a lavish tree house or a ship’s cabin: dark wood panelling on windowless walls, a balcony running around them, and multicoloured hammocks suspended from the ceiling and balcony. Bright tapestries show a gold Gryffindor lion on scarlet, black Hufflepuff badger on yellow and bronze Ravenclaw eagle on blue; Slytherin green and silver are absent.
entries.model_notes: Specific refuge configuration; do not transfer windowlessness, balcony or house banners to every room state.

entries.description: Bulging bookcases, broomsticks leaning against the walls, lamps, chairs and a large wooden-cased wireless in a corner furnish the refuge, occupied by more than twenty people.
entries.model_notes: Multiple tunnel arrivals enlarge the gathering; “more than twenty” describes the initial welcome, not maximum capacity.

entries.location: Room of Requirement / adaptive refuge and bathroom
entries.description: Neville reports the refuge beginning much smaller, with one hammock and only Gryffindor hangings, then enlarging as more DA members arrived. Seamus says it creates additional hammocks as needed and added a bathroom when girls joined the nearly two-week-old refuge.
entries.model_notes: Responsive size, occupancy furniture and sanitation, not fixed bathroom dimensions or a stable total hammock count.

entries.location: Room of Requirement / refuge access and food limits
entries.description: Seamus says the refuge remains inaccessible to the Carrows while one defender stays inside, provided the request excludes Carrow supporters and closes loopholes. Neville says that after about a day and a half of hunger the Room created the Hog’s Head passage, through which Aberforth supplies food; the Room itself does not produce food.
entries.model_notes: Request-specific access rule and workaround for food exception; refuge tunnel has existed about two weeks, despite its worn appearance.

entries.location: Room of Requirement cupboard → changing castle exit
entries.description: A small cupboard in a corner opens onto a steep, long torchlit staircase with unexpected bends. Neville says its endpoint changes daily. Harry and Luna climb to apparent solid wall, push it so it melts away, and emerge into a dark fifth-floor corridor; it reseals immediately.
entries.model_notes: Fifth floor is this evening’s exit, not a permanent corridor connection or proof that the refuge occupies a lower fixed floor.

entries.description: With Filch a corridor ahead, Harry and Luna traverse moonlit squares, corners and suits of armour whose helmets creak at their footsteps, pausing for two passing ghosts. Luna leads them onto a spiral staircase, which rises in tight dizzying circles to Ravenclaw’s door.
entries.model_notes: No count of floors, turns, armour suits or total stairs supplied; the Map gives only the starting fifth floor.

entries.description: The entrance is aged wood with neither handle nor keyhole, only a bronze eagle knocker. A knock makes its beak speak musically and ask a question. Luna says a wrong answer requires waiting for somebody who answers correctly; her answer about a circle’s lack of beginning opens it.
entries.model_notes: Reasoning challenge rather than a fixed password; one observed question does not define its entire set of questions.

entries.description: The wide circular room is exceptionally airy, with graceful arched windows between blue-and-bronze silk wall hangings. Surrounding mountains can be seen by day. A domed ceiling painted with stars is echoed by the midnight-blue carpet; tables, chairs and bookcases occupy the room.
entries.model_notes: Night visit with narrated daytime view potential. No window count, compass orientation or room diameter.

entries.location: Ravenclaw common room / Rowena statue and adjoining door
entries.description: Opposite the entrance, a niche contains a tall white-marble statue of Rowena Ravenclaw on a plinth. Beside it is a door Harry guesses leads to dormitories above. The statue has a beautiful, slightly intimidating quizzical half-smile and a delicate marble circlet etched with the motto “Wit beyond measure is man’s greatest treasure.”
entries.model_notes: Dormitory destination and upward relation are Harry’s guess, distinct from directly observed niche/door placement. Circlet replica supplies the visible diadem shape, not a claim that the actual object is here.

entries.description: Alecto’s fall rattles glass in bookcases; the ceiling trembles with running feet from sleepers above, who enter through the dormitory door. Students retreat back up the staircase to their beds.
entries.model_notes: Confirms the previous chapter’s guessed dormitories above and stair access. Bookcases have glass fronts.

entries.description: Amycus cannot open the door by shouting, shaking or loud bangs. McGonagall answers the eagle’s question about vanished objects with an explanation of non-being, and the door opens. She says Flitwick previously admitted Alecto at Amycus’s request.
entries.model_notes: Correct reasoning admits a non-Ravenclaw teacher. Prior admission of Alecto is McGonagall’s report; no house-only enchantment is established.

entries.location: Ravenclaw common room / battle damage and restraint
entries.description: Amycus is thrown into a glass-fronted bookcase, smashing the glass. McGonagall binds the Carrows with silver rope and hoists their netted bodies to hang under the ceiling, here described as blue and gold.
entries.model_notes: Dated broken furniture and suspended prisoners. Preserve this blue-and-gold ceiling wording alongside the preceding star-painted dome and bronze wall silks rather than silently standardising colours.

entries.description: McGonagall says the Floo Network is watched and Apparition impossible within the grounds. Harry proposes evacuating through the Hog’s Head tunnel and Disapparating from that pub while attackers focus on school boundaries.
entries.model_notes: Grounds prohibition and observed town street failure do not preclude the specifically proposed pub transport endpoint. Evacuation concerns hundreds of students.

entries.location: Ravenclaw spiral stair → lower corridor / unnamed classroom
entries.description: The group descends the spiral staircase and travels along corridors, then descends two additional floors before meeting Snape concealed behind armour. A wall torch sits in a bracket. Snape flees through a classroom door farther along that corridor and escapes through its window, flying towards the perimeter wall.
entries.model_notes: Do not equate “two more floors” with a surveyed tower height. The classroom is unnamed; view establishes line of sight towards the perimeter.

entries.location: Unnamed corridor and classroom / duel damage
entries.description: The torch is pulled from its wall bracket and transformed into a corridor-filling ring of fire, then serpent, smoke and daggers. Daggers pierce a suit of armour, which is animated, hurled against the wall and shattered. Snape leaves a body-shaped hole in the classroom window.
entries.model_notes: Dated magical transformations and broken fittings, not permanent materials of corridor structure.

entries.description: From the broken classroom window Flitwick directs complex protective incantations into the grounds, producing a rushing sound like wind; Protego horribilis is named. The teachers expect to delay Voldemort rather than exclude him indefinitely.
entries.model_notes: Sprout’s named plants are planned weapons at this point, not observed planted barricades.

entries.location: Castle statues and suits of armour
entries.description: McGonagall animates statues and armour along the corridor, with echoing crashes indicating the same on floors above and below, and orders them to man the boundaries. They leave their plinths, including figures smaller and larger than life and animals; the armour carries swords and spiked balls on chains.
entries.model_notes: Records original plinth-mounted displays and mobilised battle state. Activation elsewhere is inferred by Harry from sound and is described as such.

entries.location: Room of Requirement / refuge return and bathroom
entries.description: Harry and Luna return from the next staircase to the enchanted wall, which opens when Harry leans against it, and descend the steep staircase into a now densely crowded refuge. The open doorway to its bathroom leads directly off the Room; Harry finds it empty.
entries.model_notes: Demonstrates bidirectional return through the same evening’s castle exit and direct bathroom connection. Repeated arrivals use the separate Hog’s Head tunnel.

entries.description: Harry’s final vision looks through high wrought-iron gates flanked by pillars carrying winged boars, across dark grounds to the castle blazing with lights.
entries.model_notes: Gate material, flanking ornaments and castle sightline; change from unlit pre-dawn windows in chapter 24 reflects a different night/state.

entries.description: The enchanted ceiling is dark with stars above four long house tables and benches. School ghosts shine pearly white among students. McGonagall addresses them from the raised platform at the top of the Hall, with teachers and Order members behind her. Harry walks alongside the Gryffindor table; Slytherins leave on the other side of the Hall.
entries.temporal: May 1998, Battle of Hogwarts before and just after midnight
entries.model_notes: Opposite-side relationship in this scene, not a complete surveyed table order. Platform supports an assembly rather than a newly installed structure.

entries.description: Voldemort’s disembodied voice seems to issue from the Great Hall walls. Hagrid reports hearing the ultimatum in his mountain cave, and Aberforth says all Hogsmeade heard it.
entries.temporal: May 1998, Battle of Hogwarts before and just after midnight
entries.model_notes: Observed Hall sound with reported wider reach; not ordinary acoustic proof of physical proximity between cave, pub and castle.

entries.location: Astronomy, Ravenclaw and Gryffindor towers / siege positions
entries.description: Kingsley names Ravenclaw, Astronomy and Gryffindor as the three highest towers and assigns defenders there for their good overview and spell-casting positions, with other groups covering the grounds and passage entrances.
entries.temporal: May 1998, Battle of Hogwarts before and just after midnight
entries.model_notes: Names the three highest without ranking them individually here; previous highest-Astronomy evidence remains separate.

entries.location: Great Hall → Entrance Hall → marble stairs → refuge evacuation route
entries.description: Evacuees fill the Entrance Hall beyond the Great Hall and move up the marble staircase towards the Room of Requirement. At the top Harry follows a deserted corridor and sits on an empty statue plinth halfway along a passage, then returns to the stairs and descends to Nick below. Hundreds continue towards the refuge; Aberforth later reports hundreds passing through his pub.
entries.temporal: May 1998, Battle of Hogwarts before and just after midnight
entries.model_notes: Local sequence and flows, not an exact floor-to-floor survey. Vacant plinth follows the statue mobilisation.

entries.location: Entrance Hall / adjoining corridor and ghosts
entries.description: The Grey Lady crosses a solid wall from the Entrance Hall into a corridor Harry reaches through its door, then glides a few inches above the floor. She is tall, with waist-length hair and a floor-length cloak; she identifies herself as Helena Ravenclaw. She shows the dark wound in her chest and says the Bloody Baron wears chains in penitence.
entries.temporal: May 1998, Battle of Hogwarts before and just after midnight
entries.model_notes: Observed ghost appearance and wall passage; Baron-chain explanation is her report. Her Albanian forest and hollow tree are remote and not Hogwarts vegetation.

entries.description: Harry deduces that Riddle hid the diadem during his visit to request a teaching job, on the way to or from Dumbledore’s office.
entries.temporal: May 1998, Battle of Hogwarts before and just after midnight
entries.model_notes: Reasoning links the hiding room to the remembered job interview, without proving an exact route or time of placement.

entries.description: Hagrid reports Grawp carrying him and Fang from their cave, smashing through the boundary by the Forest and putting them through a castle window. Harry sees Hagrid crash through a window to his left into the opposite corridor wall, with Grawp outside. Hagrid’s later footfalls shake the corridor’s floorboards.
entries.temporal: May 1998, Battle of Hogwarts before and just after midnight
entries.model_notes: Dated breach and wooden corridor floor; boundary material and height of this window are not given.

entries.description: Two stone gargoyles normally guarding the staff-room entrance are smashed by a jinx entering through a broken window. Their fragments still stir and one detached head speaks from the floor.
entries.temporal: May 1998, Battle of Hogwarts before and just after midnight
entries.model_notes: Establishes paired stone guardians and damaged animated remnants, without identifying floor or side of doorway.

entries.description: Sprout, Neville and about half a dozen others carry large potted Mandrakes while wearing earmuffs. Neville says they intend to throw them over the walls.
entries.temporal: May 1998, Battle of Hogwarts before and just after midnight
entries.model_notes: Observed plants and ear protection; deployment over a particular wall is still intended, not seen here.

entries.location: Castle portraits / news network and Sir Cadogan
entries.description: Painted figures in historical dress race alongside Harry through neighbouring canvases, cramming into each other’s pictures and shouting news from elsewhere in the castle. Sir Cadogan, a small armoured knight with a fat pony, accompanies him from frame to frame along one corridor.
entries.temporal: May 1998, Battle of Hogwarts before and just after midnight
entries.model_notes: Within-castle portrait movement and information flow. No frame dimensions or permanent hanging order supplied.

entries.location: Castle passages / vase and displaced display statue
entries.description: A huge vase explodes from its plinth as the castle shakes. In another corridor Fred’s group guards a concealed hole beside an empty plinth whose former statue hid a secret passage; owls crowd a subsequent corridor.
entries.temporal: May 1998, Battle of Hogwarts before and just after midnight
entries.model_notes: Do not identify this unnamed statue passage with a known named tunnel without cross-book evidence. Owls’ presence does not locate the Owlery.

entries.location: Chamber of Secrets / entry and Basilisk remains
entries.description: Ron and Hermione report visiting the Chamber, tearing great curved dirty-yellow fangs from the dead Basilisk’s skull and using one to destroy the cup. Ron opened the entrance by imitating Harry’s Parseltongue command after several attempts.
entries.temporal: May 1998, Battle of Hogwarts before and just after midnight
entries.model_notes: The required sound can be reproduced without natural Parseltongue ability; no new entrance geometry or proof of every remaining skeleton element.

entries.location: Room of Requirement / refuge exit and tunnel closure
entries.description: Harry leads the trio down the concealed staircase into the almost-empty refuge. He knows the Room cannot transform while users remain inside. Augusta says she was the last through the Hog’s Head passage and sealed it after Aberforth left; the last refuge occupants then leave by the stone steps.
entries.temporal: May 1998, Battle of Hogwarts before and just after midnight
entries.model_notes: Reported sealing method unspecified. Physical stair exit and later three-pass hiding-room entrance are narrated separately; do not force the variable refuge route into one fixed plan.

entries.description: Ron expects the house-elves to be down in the kitchen during the battle and urges warning them to escape.
entries.temporal: May 1998, Battle of Hogwarts before and just after midnight
entries.model_notes: Expectation of occupied kitchen, not a witnessed headcount or an evacuation that is shown taking place.

entries.location: Corridor windows / castle foot / North Battlements
entries.description: Back upstairs dust fills shaking corridors. Through one window Harry sees fighting flashes close to the castle’s foot and Grawp carrying what looks like a roof-torn stone gargoyle. At the next window, missing several panes, Ginny casts into fighters below. Aberforth reports enemy giants apparently breaching the North Battlements.
entries.temporal: May 1998, Battle of Hogwarts before and just after midnight
entries.model_notes: North is explicit for battlements, not necessarily for these windows. Gargoyle origin and breach are qualified observations/reports, not surveyed facts.

entries.location: Room of Requirement / hidden-things entrance and acoustic isolation
entries.description: Harry’s mental request for the place where everything is hidden makes a door appear on the third pass along its wall. Closing it silences the battle; the huge room produces echoes. Hermione’s Summoning Charm fails to bring the diadem.
entries.temporal: May 1998, Battle of Hogwarts before and just after midnight
entries.model_notes: One failed object-summoning attempt does not establish that all charms always fail throughout the Room. Hidden-things state is available after the refuge empties.

entries.location: Room of Hidden Things / scale, contents and landmarks
entries.description: The cathedral-sized space resembles a city with towering walls of hidden objects and aisles between them. Harry passes the stuffed troll and the Vanishing Cabinet Malfoy repaired. Piles contain bottles, hats, crates, chairs, books, weapons, broomsticks and bats; one junk wall of old furniture, broken trunks, books and robes is fifty feet high. A three-legged wardrobe and a tower of desks also provide cover.
entries.temporal: May 1998, Battle of Hogwarts before and just after midnight
entries.model_notes: Fifty feet belongs to a particular heap, not the ceiling height. Aisle to Harry’s right contains Ron behind a junk wall; speech becomes inaudible at greater distance.

entries.description: A blistered old cupboard holds Harry’s old Potions book. On top stands a pockmarked stone effigy of an ugly old warlock wearing a dusty wig and an ancient discoloured tiara. Harry recognises this marker from his previous visit, and identifies the tiara as the lost diadem.
entries.temporal: May 1998, Battle of Hogwarts before and just after midnight
entries.model_notes: Same marker group as book 6; discovery establishes the identity that was not then known. Harry is ten feet away when interrupted, not a measurement of cupboard height.

entries.location: Room of Hidden Things / duel destabilisation
entries.description: Crabbe’s Descendo makes a fifty-foot junk wall crumble into the adjacent aisle; Harry steadies it with Finite. A later curse blasts the stone bust into the air, sending the diadem into the heap below.
entries.temporal: May 1998, Battle of Hogwarts before and just after midnight
entries.model_notes: Dated changes before the fire, preserving the marker’s loss rather than leaving it standing afterward.

entries.location: Room of Hidden Things / Fiendfyre destruction
entries.description: Crabbe’s cursed fire climbs heaps that turn to soot, evaporates Harry’s water jet, pursues the fugitives and forms huge fiery serpents, Chimaeras, dragons and a birdlike raptor. It consumes and throws objects high into dense black smoke and overwhelming heat. Harry and his friends use two stored broomsticks to fly above it, rescuing Malfoy and Goyle from charred desks.
entries.temporal: May 1998, Battle of Hogwarts before and just after midnight
entries.model_notes: Hermione identifies it as Fiendfyre. Destruction of much stored material is explicit; complete destruction of every item or every future room configuration is not proved.

entries.location: Room of Requirement / escape aperture and uncertain future usability
entries.description: Harry sees the doorway as a rectangular patch through smoke and flies through it, colliding with the corridor wall beyond. The door has vanished when the survivors sit outside. Ron questions whether the Room will still work after the fire.
entries.model_notes: Do not turn an unanswered question into a permanent closure claim. The Headless Hunt subsequently gallops through the corridor on ghostly horses, carrying their heads beneath their arms.

entries.location: Ravenclaw diadem / destruction outside hiding room
entries.description: The recovered old diadem is blackened and hot, its tiny wisdom motto still legible. A dark tarry fluid leaks out before it vibrates and breaks into fragments in Harry’s hands.
entries.temporal: May 1998, Battle of Hogwarts before and just after midnight
entries.model_notes: Dated destruction of the formerly stored object; its material is not specified in these paragraphs.

entries.location: Corridor outside Room of Requirement / exploded outer wall
entries.description: Death Eaters enter the castle and duel in the corridor. An explosion throws the group into rubble, blowing away part of the castle’s outer side and admitting cold air. Harry and Hermione stumble over stone and wood beside the blasted wall, where Fred has been killed.
entries.temporal: May 1998, Battle of Hogwarts before and just after midnight
entries.model_notes: No named floor or explicit source of this particular explosion. Keep this damage distinct from the Room’s fire.

entries.description: Curses and a falling body pass the large outer-wall breach. Car-sized giant spiders climb the castle side and try to enter through it. Fred is hidden in a niche formerly occupied by armour; farther along, dust and falling masonry fill a corridor whose windows have lost their glass.
entries.model_notes: Aragog’s descendants are identified in narration. Death Eater penetration of their Forest is Harry’s inference; exact exterior wall orientation remains unknown.

entries.location: Concealed stair / two tapestries / lower corridor
entries.description: Behind the tapestry where Hermione restrains Ron is a staircase with concealing tapestries at top and bottom. Glisseo flattens it into a chute and the trio slide through the lower tapestry to the opposite wall. Hermione turns that tapestry to stone with Duro, stopping the pursuing Death Eaters; a nearby door shelters the trio as McGonagall drives animated desks past.
entries.model_notes: Specific temporary slide and stone obstruction, not permanent stair design. No named floor or identified relationship to earlier tapestry shortcuts.

entries.location: Lower corridor → marble staircase / active plant weapons
entries.description: After another descending staircase they reach a corridor full of duellers and portraits crowded with advisers. Peeves flies overhead dropping Snargaluff pods, whose green wormlike roots engulf heads and spill slippery juice. The trio run through it to the upper landing of the marble staircase leading into the Entrance Hall.
entries.model_notes: Concrete travel sequence and battle surface hazard. Neville carries Venomous Tentacula into the Hall, where it coils around and reels in an enemy.

entries.location: Entrance Hall / hourglass, balcony, marble banisters and doors
entries.description: As the trio descend the marble stairs, the Slytherin points hourglass shatters on their left and spills emeralds underfoot. Two bodies fall from a balcony overhead. Greyback is thrown into marble banisters; Trelawney attacks from above them with crystal balls, one smashing a window across the Hall. Heavy wooden front doors burst open for giant spiders.
entries.model_notes: Slytherin hourglass, not the previously broken Gryffindor one. “Left” is relative to descent, with no compass direction or complete arrangement of house clocks.

entries.location: Castle front steps / giant attack / upper window
entries.description: Outside the front steps a twenty-foot giant is illuminated at its shins by light from the castle doors; it smashes an upper window and reaches through for people. Harry shelters in the doorway from falling glass. Grawp rounds a castle corner, fights it beside trembling stone steps, and the trio run down into the grounds towards the Forest.
entries.model_notes: Visible scale and reach, without assigning a numbered floor to the broken window. Grawp is smaller than this enemy giant.

entries.location: Grounds between castle and Forest / Dementor wave and giant
entries.description: Halfway towards the Forest the trio meet about a hundred Dementors advancing towards the castle. Their cold freezes breath and muffles battle sounds; Patronuses scatter them and warmth and normal volume return. Another giant emerges from the Forest direction carrying a club taller than the students, forcing them to run towards the Whomping Willow.
entries.model_notes: Approximate encounter midpoint and directional origin, no measured separation between Forest and Willow.

entries.description: While running to the Willow, Harry hears the lake crashing like the sea and the Forbidden Forest creaking despite a windless night, as though the grounds themselves are in rebellion.
entries.model_notes: Dated magical or battle disturbance; no ordinary-weather explanation or permanent rough-lake condition implied.

entries.location: Whomping Willow / root entrance and disabling knot
entries.description: Whip-like branches defend the secret at the old Willow’s roots. A single knot in the bark near the roots paralyses the tree when jabbed. Ron levitates a fallen twig through its branches to touch that spot, making it still.
entries.model_notes: Remote physical pressure works; no need for a person or animal to touch the knot directly. Keep knot low near roots, without inventing its exact side.

entries.description: The earthy passage hidden among the roots has a low ceiling: where they once had to stoop four years earlier, the older trio must now crawl. It runs without any encountered barriers, then slopes upwards towards light. A crate blocks its final opening into the Shack room, leaving a small viewing gap against the wall; Harry levitates it an inch up and sideways to enter.
entries.model_notes: Observed navigability differs from the earlier general claim that old passages were all sealed; preserve rather than silently resolve that discrepancy. No exact length, bearing or numbered Shack floor supplied.

entries.location: Shrieking Shack / occupied room and castle view
entries.description: The desolate room has peeling wallpaper, boarded windows except one, and a solitary oil lamp. Its open window shows distant battle flashes at the castle, whose sounds are muffled. Lucius sits in its darkest corner. At the tunnel end Harry can see the edge of a table with Voldemort beside it; Snape passes within inches of the concealed opening.
entries.model_notes: Room identified by Harry after the vision and then reached physically. Visibility from a tunnel gap is restricted, so do not infer a complete furnishing inventory.

entries.description: Nagini floats and coils in a transparent starry sphere, described as between a cage and tank. Voldemort moves it through the air to enclose Snape’s head and shoulders so the snake can attack; Snape cannot push it off. The sphere then lifts free and follows Voldemort out, leaving Snape on the floor.
entries.model_notes: Temporary movable magical containment, not a built feature of the Shack. Physical force does not remove it in the observed attack; other counters are not tested.

entries.description: Voldemort’s voice reverberates from the Shack walls and floor with the intimacy of someone standing beside the listeners. Harry understands it is being heard equally clearly at Hogwarts and throughout the surrounding area, including Hogsmeade.
entries.model_notes: Wide-area magical sound during the one-hour retreat; not an ordinary room-acoustic relationship.

entries.location: Willow tunnel → front lawn → castle steps
entries.description: The trio crawl back through the tunnel and hurry towards the castle stone steps. Small bundles litter the front lawn in near-dawn darkness, and an abandoned giant’s clog, like a small boat, lies there; the giants themselves are absent.
entries.model_notes: Bundles are not identified individually. The text jumps from tunnel transit to front lawn without surveying the intervening grounds route.

entries.description: The deserted, silent Entrance Hall has blood-stained flagstones, scattered emeralds, broken marble and splintered wood. Part of the banisters has been blasted away.
entries.model_notes: Continues chapter 32’s points-clock and stair damage, adding broken banisters and debris materials.

entries.location: Great Hall / casualty and treatment configuration
entries.description: The house tables have been removed. Survivors gather in groups, the injured are treated by Pomfrey and helpers on the raised platform, and the dead lie in a row through the middle. Remus and Tonks lie beside Fred beneath the dark enchanted ceiling.
entries.model_notes: Dated cleared floor and triage platform, distinct from the earlier seated assembly; no disposal or restoration method for tables stated.

entries.description: Harry turns from the Great Hall doorway, runs up the marble staircase and through the empty castle to the stone gargoyle. Saying Dumbledore makes it slide aside and reveal the spiral staircase to the circular office.
entries.model_notes: Password works at this time; not proof of a permanent password or a measured direct stair connection from Entrance Hall to office.

entries.location: Headmaster’s office / portraits, chair and Pensieve
entries.description: Portraits hang all around the circular office, now empty; Dumbledore’s deserted frame is directly behind the Headmaster’s chair. The stone Pensieve is kept in its cabinet and is lifted onto the desk. Its wide basin has runic markings around the edge, and the office floor is carpeted.
entries.model_notes: Narration speculates that absent headmasters are watching battle events through castle pictures; absence is directly seen but their exact destinations are not.

entries.description: At platform nine and three-quarters students load trunks aboard the scarlet steam engine, carrying cats and caged owls. On the countryside journey a corridor serves compartments with sliding doors, facing seats and window-side corner seating.
entries.model_notes: Historical school transport geometry; London platform is retained only as the school railway’s departure context, not a separate city model.

entries.description: Candlelit house tables and benches face the Sorting area with a rickety stool on which the Hat is placed on each child. Lily joins Gryffindor; Snape moves to the other side of the Hall to sit with Slytherin.
entries.model_notes: Corroborates opposite-side Gryffindor/Slytherin seating decades earlier; no intervening table order or precise stool placement.

entries.description: Lily and Snape cross the castle courtyard while arguing; Lily stops and leans against a pillar.
entries.temporal: School years in the mid-1970s, exact year not specified
entries.model_notes: An unnamed courtyard contains at least one pillar; no covered walkway, cloister, shape or dimension supplied.

entries.description: Lily reports Snape going down the tunnel by the Whomping Willow and James saving him from what was below; the preceding conversation mentions Lupin’s full-moon absences.
entries.model_notes: Historical use and danger; do not add a new trap, chamber or new geometry not stated in the conversation.

entries.description: After his Defence O.W.L. in the Great Hall, Snape walks away from the castle and inadvertently nears a beech tree under which James, Sirius, Lupin and Pettigrew sit.
entries.model_notes: Tree species and exam-to-grounds sequence; no lake relationship is stated in this paragraph.

entries.description: At night Lily stands in a corridor before the Fat Lady’s portrait at the Gryffindor Tower entrance, then climbs back through the portrait hole, leaving Snape outside.
entries.model_notes: Shows the same type of portrait entrance in an earlier generation; no newly specified floor or password.

entries.description: Dumbledore and Snape speak apart in the Entrance Hall as the last Yule Ball guests pass towards bed; Fleur and Roger Davies come in from the grounds and continue past them.
entries.model_notes: Grounds-to-Hall and onward sleeping-area circulation, without assuming a specifically named exterior door or bedroom destination.

entries.location: Headmaster’s office / desk chairs and objects
entries.description: Dumbledore occupies a throne-like chair behind the desk, with a visitor’s chair across from him. The cracked Gaunt ring and Gryffindor sword lie together on the desk. Fawkes is present, audibly gnawing cuttlebone.
entries.temporal: Memories spanning 1981, 1991 and summer 1996; detailed desk scene summer 1996
entries.model_notes: Earlier office scenes corroborate seating but the throne-like shape, opposite guest chair and ring/sword layout belong to the 1996 treatment scene, not every year.

entries.description: In a later night office conversation, with dark windows and Fawkes sitting silently, Snape’s silver doe lands on the floor, bounds across the office and soars out of the window as Dumbledore watches.
entries.model_notes: A visible outward window route for a Patronus, not proof a solid body could pass without opening the window. No compass direction given.

entries.location: Headmaster’s office / portrait communication under Snape
entries.description: Snape consults Dumbledore’s portrait behind his desk. Phineas returns into his school frame with a location heard when Hermione opened her handbag, and Dumbledore’s portrait speaks from behind the Headmaster’s chair.
entries.model_notes: Confirms functioning Dumbledore portrait and Phineas’s listening through the portable frame; it was the open bag that exposed the location.

entries.location: Headmaster’s office / hidden cavity behind Dumbledore’s portrait
entries.description: Snape pulls the side of Dumbledore’s portrait so it swings forwards, exposing a hidden cavity behind it from which he takes the real sword of Gryffindor before leaving through the office door.
entries.model_notes: Physical concealed sword store behind a movable portrait, directly observed through memory. Its construction date and dimensions are unspecified; this resolves the real sword’s storage before delivery, not the timing of the display-case substitution.

entries.location: Headmaster’s office → Entrance Hall → front grounds
entries.description: Harry leaves the dusty carpeted office with portraits still absent, descends through the floors to the marble staircase, crosses the Entrance Hall and exits by the front doors and steps. Neville and Wood bring a body in from the grounds to the Great Hall; the grounds nearby hold other dead and wounded.
entries.temporal: May 1998, near four in the morning during the ceasefire
entries.model_notes: Narrated uninterrupted route but no turn or floor count. Near-four-o’clock timing is explicit.

entries.location: Front grounds → Hagrid’s hut → Forbidden Forest edge
entries.description: Continuing away from the castle, Harry passes Hagrid’s hut, dark and silent, then reaches the Forest edge. The hut recalls a copper kettle shining on the fire, rock cakes and giant grubs from earlier visits.
entries.temporal: May 1998, near four in the morning during the ceasefire
entries.model_notes: Confirms the hut is standing during this battle after book 6’s fire, without supplying the rebuilding history or exact distance from castle/Forest.

entries.location: Forbidden Forest outer edge / Dementors and terrain
entries.description: Earthy, twig-strewn ground marks the outer Forest edge. Dementors glide among the trees, bringing chill. A cold breeze seems to issue from deeper in the Forest.
entries.temporal: May 1998, near four in the morning during the ceasefire
entries.model_notes: Local terrain and dated enemy presence; breeze attribution is qualified by the narration.

entries.description: Harry proceeds deeper through old trees growing close together, with tangled branches and gnarled twisted roots underfoot. He stumbles and slips; a pair of patrolling Death Eaters emerge from behind a nearby tree, then lead him farther in.
entries.temporal: May 1998, near four in the morning during the ceasefire
entries.model_notes: Natural obstacles and dense woodland, without a named established path or a compass bearing. Dolohov’s statement about Hagrid keeping creatures there is a character report.

entries.location: Forbidden Forest / Resurrection Stone effects and loss
entries.description: At the Forest edge Harry turns the Stone three times and sees his dead parents, Sirius and Lupin, more substantial than ghosts but less than living bodies. They are invisible to others and shield him emotionally from Dementors like Patronuses. On entering the clearing’s firelight he drops the Stone and they vanish.
entries.temporal: May 1998, near four in the morning during the ceasefire
entries.model_notes: Dated supernatural companions and lost object at the approach to the clearing; no exact drop coordinates or persistent visible figures afterward.

entries.location: Aragog’s former clearing / Death Eater camp
entries.description: After only minutes following the patrol deeper in, Harry reaches the clearing where Aragog lived. Remnants of his vast web remain, but the descendants have been driven out to fight. A fire burns in the centre, surrounded by silent Death Eaters; two giants sit at the group’s outskirts, casting huge shadows.
entries.temporal: May 1998, near four in the morning during the ceasefire
entries.model_notes: Relative few-minute final segment, not total castle-to-clearing travel time. Dated occupation and reduced spider presence.

entries.location: Forest clearing / Voldemort, fire, protective sphere and prisoner tree
entries.description: Voldemort stands beyond the fire with Nagini’s glittering sphere floating behind his head. Bellatrix sits closest to him. Harry enters the firelight and faces him across only the fire; Hagrid is bound to a nearby tree, his struggles shaking its branches.
entries.temporal: May 1998, near four in the morning during the ceasefire
entries.model_notes: Local staging for this confrontation, no fixed camp architecture. Tree species, direction and precise separation are unstated.

entries.location: Forest clearing → thinning trees → outer edge
entries.description: Harry lies on cold hard ground in the clearing, then Hagrid carries him through close-growing trees whose branches catch his hair and robes. The two following giants knock trees over, disturbing shrieking birds. The trees gradually thin towards open ground; centaurs watch before the party reaches the fresh air of the edge, where Dementors patrol the outer trees.
entries.model_notes: Return-route vegetation gradient and dated tree destruction; Hagrid’s words establish watching centaurs without a witnessed number.

entries.location: Forest edge → castle front lawn and steps
entries.description: Voldemort magnifies his voice through the grounds from the Forest edge, then leads the procession towards the castle. The Death Eaters form a line facing its open front doors, lit red by light from the Entrance Hall; defenders fill the doorway and front steps. Harry is lowered onto grass at Voldemort’s feet between the opposing groups.
entries.model_notes: Front lawn, lit Hall sightline and open staging, without measured distances. Nagini has been released from her protective sphere and rides Voldemort’s shoulders.

entries.location: Castle window / Sorting Hat during confrontation
entries.description: Voldemort summons the ragged, empty, mildewed Sorting Hat from a shattered castle window, places it on Neville and ignites it. Neville breaks free of his binding curse and draws a silver sword with a glittering rubied handle from the flaming Hat, then beheads Nagini.
entries.model_notes: Air route of a summoned object, not proof of office window location. Announced abolition of houses is Voldemort’s intention, not an observed redecoration.

entries.description: Uproar comes from the distant, out-of-sight boundary walls as what sounds like hundreds climb over and run towards the castle. Grawp rounds the castle side; enemy giants rush him while charging centaurs fire arrows. Thestrals and Buckbeak attack the giants’ eyes from the air, and the fighters are driven back into the castle.
entries.model_notes: Wall crossing is initially heard and interpreted rather than seen. Later arrivals appear to include Hogsmeade residents and fighters’ families under Charlie and Slughorn; no particular gate used is stated.

entries.location: Front steps → Entrance Hall → Great Hall / kitchen route
entries.description: The crowd enters through the front doors and Harry is swept into the Entrance Hall, where Voldemort backs across into the Great Hall. Further reinforcements climb the front steps, centaurs enter, and the door leading to the kitchens is blasted off its hinges as armed house-elves swarm into the Entrance Hall.
entries.model_notes: Kitchen-route door connects with the Entrance Hall circulation, but does not establish that the kitchen room itself directly adjoins it without intervening stairs/passages.

entries.location: Great Hall / final duels and floor damage
entries.description: Crowds fill the Great Hall and hundreds line its walls around the last two fights. Voldemort and Bellatrix duel about fifty yards apart. Hagrid throws Macnair against a stone wall. Molly and Bellatrix’s spells heat and crack the floor around their feet.
entries.model_notes: Fifty-yard distance is between duellists in this scene, establishing a substantial room span but not its exact length or width.

entries.location: Great Hall / dawn window and enchanted ceiling
entries.description: A red-gold glow crosses the enchanted ceiling as dazzling sunlight appears over the nearest window sill, striking Harry’s and Voldemort’s faces simultaneously. The Elder Wand spins across that sky-like ceiling against the sunrise; the rising sun then dazzles the windows and fills the Hall with light.
entries.model_notes: Useful sunrise sightline; no explicit compass orientation or identification of which wall carries this window.

entries.location: Great Hall / house tables restored and adjacent chamber
entries.description: Voldemort’s body is placed in a chamber off the Hall, apart from the fallen defenders. McGonagall restores the house tables and benches, though people sit mingled across houses and species. Firenze recovers in a corner. Grawp peers through a smashed window while people throw him food, and aisles remain between tables.
entries.model_notes: Post-battle communal configuration and an unnamed adjoining chamber; broken window permits Grawp’s face and food exchange without fixing his stance or window height.

entries.location: Great Hall → damaged marble stairs → office approach
entries.description: The trio leave the Hall and climb marble stairs missing large chunks and part of the balustrade, with rubble and bloodstains every few steps. They continue through a doorway and along the castle route to the office, hearing Peeves’s victory song in distant corridors.
entries.model_notes: Damage remains after table restoration. No wholesale castle repair is narrated.

entries.location: Headmaster’s office / displaced gargoyle and moving staircase
entries.description: The guarding gargoyle has been knocked aside and stands lopsided. It grants access conversationally; the trio climb over it onto the spiral stone staircase, which moves slowly upward like an escalator, then pass through the door at the top.
entries.model_notes: Current access bypasses the normal password request. Harry’s doubt whether it can distinguish passwords is speculation, not a diagnosed permanent loss.

entries.location: Headmaster’s office / returned portraits and desk
entries.description: The Pensieve still stands on the desk where Harry left it. The returned heads’ portraits surround the walls, their subjects standing on painted chairs and reaching between frames to shake hands. Dilys Derwent weeps, Dexter Fortescue waves an ear-trumpet and Phineas calls out; Dumbledore occupies the largest portrait directly behind the Headmaster’s chair.
entries.model_notes: Returned subjects and comparative frame size, with desk still usable. The portraits’ chairs are painted contents, not real chairs along the office walls.

entries.location: Forbidden Forest / lost Stone and proposed tomb return
entries.description: Harry tells Dumbledore’s portrait that he dropped the Stone in the Forest and does not know exactly where. He intends to leave it unsearched, and to put the Elder Wand back where it came from.
entries.model_notes: Location discussion after the battle does not depict a completed return of the wand or a repaired tomb. Earlier chapters identify the wand’s source as Dumbledore’s tomb.

entries.description: As he leaves the office conversation, Harry thinks of the four-poster bed awaiting him in Gryffindor Tower and of asking Kreacher to bring a sandwich there.
entries.model_notes: Expected sleeping furniture and tower destination, not a narrated post-battle visit or a confirmed food delivery.

entries.description: Families pass through the barrier between platforms nine and ten without collision to reach platform nine and three-quarters, clouded by thick white steam from the scarlet Hogwarts Express. Carriages have doors and opening windows, with a corridor along which James runs; the train leaves near eleven and rounds a corner out of sight.
entries.model_notes: School railway departure endpoint only; the fifty-yard separation of families on the platform is not a Hogwarts grounds measurement. No Hogsmeade station arrival is depicted in the epilogue.

entries.description: Harry tells first-year Albus he will go up to school in the boats rather than the carriages. James warns him about Thestrals, which Albus says James described as invisible; Harry calls them gentle.
entries.model_notes: Confirms the two arrival modes remain in use nineteen years after the battle. No launch site, lake course, carriage road or universal visibility rule is supplied here.
